approach: Root cause: files kept by hand as mirrors of a governing source (xtask/shard-timings.txt, docs/decisions.md, the CI athena-bin cache key vs status::BUILD_PATHS, docs/ontology.toml) are tested for structure only, or checked late, so content that contradicts the source passes until the final verdict. Fix at the origin: one registry in new crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs. Each entry names a mirror file, a described source (path, glob, constant or git HEAD) and a comparison rule. Four rules: (a) every `--test` unit in xtask/shard-timings.txt matches the test files on disk, both ways; (b) docs/decisions.md starts with the exact bytes of its HEAD version; (c) every `athena-bin` hashFiles list in ci.yml covers every status::BUILD_PATHS root; (d) in docs/ontology.toml, every line of a governing doc that names a term as a definition or role is covered by a sense or excuse. One source of truth per rule (revision): rule (d) reuses the ontology matching helpers by moving them from crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs into mirrors.rs, and ontology.rs calls them. Rule (c) drops the earlier include_str! scan, because xtask/tests/policy.rs already checks the key against BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS; (c) covers only what policy.rs cannot see, the status.rs list. Rule (a) keeps its on-disk derivation, and a real-repo test checks that derivation against `cargo metadata`, the original. The run_check hook is dropped (it ran after handover, in the verifier, and could be excused as pre-existing). The before-handover call site is a producer-brief instruction in briefs.rs, modelled on BOUNDARY_SCAN_INSTRUCTION, to run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors`, with a briefs.rs unit test. A new athena-cli test target runs the registry over the real repo and, for every REGISTRY entry, over a drifted fixture, so a new entry is covered with no other edit.

decisions.choice: One registry `REGISTRY: &[Mirror]` with `Mirror { name, mirror: &str, source: Source, rule: Rule }`. `Source` is an enum (Path, Glob, Constant, GitHead) so a source that is not a path is described as what it is. `Rule` is an enum: TimingUnits, AppendOnly, HashFilesCover(&'static [&'static str]), OntologyTerms. `check_entry(entry, root, base)` and `check_all(root, base)` return `Vec<Drift>` (mirror path, message naming file and fix); `base: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` is injected.
decisions.reason: The cause is that nothing makes a mirror declare how it is compared to its source. A registry makes the declaration the unit, and the repo test iterates it, so a new entry is covered with no other edit. Pure rule fns give unit seams without git or the filesystem.

The registry rule parses docs/ontology.toml with toml_edit and calls the same `scan` and `uncovered_lines`. The sense and says check (`claim_problems` lines 320-360) stays in ontology.rs.

A ci.yml with no such key line is a drift. No include_str! scan. The rule holds `&status::BUILD_PATHS` in the Rule variant. status.rs gets a doc comment only.

A None base skips the rule. The pin PINNED_LEN/PINNED_SHA256 in crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs stays for committed history.

risks.risk: test_units diverges from cargo's real target set, for example a [[test]] entry with a custom path, giving a false drift or a false pass.

risks.risk: The append-only rule compares with HEAD, so it is trivially true once the change is committed, and it is skipped when no git repository is present (the verifier's snapshot may lack one).

Fixtures: tempfile trees, with a fixed `base` closure injected into `check_entry`. athena-cli has athena-core and tempfile (Cargo.toml lines 19 and 32). The target is added by plan step 4 and the functions by steps 1 and 2.

demonstrations.method: Grep `MIRROR_CHECK_INSTRUCTION` and `mirror_check_section` in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs to show the call site in `producer_brief_with_evidence`. The new test `producer_briefs_tell_the_producer_to_run_the_mirror_check` builds a producer brief as the neighbour test at briefs.rs line 3028 does, and asserts: it contains 'run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors`'; the text sits after '## Words you must not write' and before '## Checks Athena will run'; and the file crates/athena-cli/tests/mirrors.rs exists. `git diff` shows the CHANGELOG.md bullet and the append-only D158.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes: the producer brief carries the instruction before its checks, and the named test target exists in the repo.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the section, the brief has no mirrors instruction and the assertion on the instruction text fails. If the target file were renamed, the existence assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `briefs::producer_brief` with a `ProducerInputs` literal, as in the test at briefs.rs line 3028 (exists). No double. The section and constant are added by plan step 5.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs, each as its own simple command. The new athena-cli mirrors target, the briefs test, the moved ontology helpers (ontology.rs still passes through them) and xtask's ci_shards cover test all run inside `cargo test --locked`. Regressions: `cargo test -p athena-cli --test ontology`, `cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards`, `cargo test -p athena-core --test external_calls_guard`, `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`. No reading parser, stem list or reading check changes, so refusal_corpus is a regression run only; I did not read its case ids and did not run it.
demonstrations.observes: The whole workspace passes, including `athena-cli --test mirrors`, `athena-cli --test ontology` (same messages, now calling the shared helpers), xtask `checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit`, `decisions` (append-only pin), `budgets` and `external_calls_guard`. `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` are clean when run as separate commands.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the shard-timings line, both xtask's cover test and the mirrors real-repo test fail. If ontology.rs lost an import or a moved helper changed behavior, the ontology tests fail. A banned word or unformatted code fails policy, fmt or clippy.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: the cargo commands over the real tree. No double. The oracles are the real-repo tests (`athena-cli --test mirrors`, added by step 4; xtask ci_shards, exists at lines 411-421).
